Daily News Briefing - 2026-10-27
Topics covered: - Anthropic has formally filed to go public, and its own paperwork warns that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" if misused, weaponised or allowed to operate with high autonomy - The capital race around it intensified - On capabilities, OpenAI claims three major results: a proof of the local smoothing conjecture that would also resolve Kakeya and Stein's restriction conjecture in all dimensions, an algorithm it says refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis, and an existence proof for interacting quantum field theories including quantum chromodynamics - A separate agent-behaviour scare cooled quickly - Israelis are voting today in what the Guardian calls the most consequential election in the country's history - With Israel's count tonight and America's midterms a week away, the next few days will test whether this anti-incumbent run reaches its biggest prizes

Topics covered: - New detail has emerged about OpenAI's agents hacking outside websites during testing - There is also a sobering read on the economics - In Brazil, Lula has won a fourth term, becoming the first first-round runner-up to take the presidency since democracy returned in the nineteen-eighties - Serbia delivered a second upset - In Venezuela, María Corina Machado returned almost a year after leaving the country - Israel votes Tuesday, and the BBC says Friday's final polls showed the two blocs almost neck and neck

item.title: Daily News Briefing - 2026-10-25

Daily News Briefing - 2026-10-25
Topics covered: - With the midterms nine days away, a new study suggests the models behind America's chatbots are not politically neutral - Lawmakers are starting to respond to AI in political and commercial messaging - TechCrunch's postmortem on the PHP flaws adds nuance to the AI angle - In Ukraine, the military says its Starlink connection is stable again, ten days after speed caps of one hundred sixty kilometres per hour wrecked missions against jet-powered Shaheds - Brazil votes today in a presidential runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, whose father is serving a twenty-seven-year sentence for plotting a coup - In France, the government says at least four hundred thousand people marched in support of striking schoolchildren and against heavy policing, while unions put the figure at double that

item.title: Daily News Briefing - 2026-10-12
item.description:
Daily News Briefing - 2026-10-12
Topics covered: - Britain is preparing to tell frontier AI companies they must do more on safety - The Verge reports that Silicon Valley is adopting President Trump's push to rename artificial intelligence as "super intelligence." An executive order requires federal agencies to use the term, and Trump has called anyone who sticks with the old phrase "the enemy." Elon Musk, Marc Benioff and Jensen Huang have already gone along with the change - On Ukraine, Trump declared an "energy ceasefire" on Truth Social, saying "both parties have agreed." Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the deal was "news to me," though he would accept it if Vladimir Putin did the same - The Houthi campaign against Saudi Arabia continues - In Pakistan, President Asif Ali Zardari declared an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and suspended its government, which is run by Imran Khan's party - The day's EU sanctions vote and London's AI speech will each test how far allies are willing to break with Washington's line
